headline: Detroit Might Be Part of the GLMZ But It's Not Meridian 88
body:
Let me explain this one more time, because I have explained it many times and it keeps requiring explanation.

Yes, [[Detroit]] is inside the Great Lakes Metropolitan Zone. Yes, I carry a [[GLMZ]] zone card. Yes, my healthcare allocation comes through [[GLMZ]] Economic Zone Authority disbursement channels. I am legally, administratively, and for all official purposes a [[GLMZ]] resident. I know this. Every Detroiter knows this. We have known it since 2193 when the zone boundary was extended east to include the Michigan lower peninsula, and we did not get a vote, and we did not get additional representation on the EZA board, and we got a new line on our residency documents that reads '[[GLMZ]]/EAST' as if the slash could contain thirty years of subsequent resentment.

I am not, and have never been, from [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]].

[[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] is the western shore. It is the infrastructure corridor running north from what used to be [[Chicago]] through Milwaukee and [[Lambeau Terminus|Green Bay]] to the Canadian frontier. It is built along the 88th meridian west, a line of longitude that runs approximately 200 kilometers west of where I am sitting right now. The corridor's transit spines, data arteries, power grids, and cultural identity were built by and for the people who live along that specific longitudinal spine. They named their city. The name belongs to them. It does not extend east of the lake by implication, by administrative boundary, or by any other mechanism, and I did not ask for it.

I raise this again because last week a music journalist from the [[Iron Meridian Cooperative Backbone IMC-3 'Spine'|Spine]] — 'from the 88,' as she kept saying, with the warmth of someone who lives inside something they love — asked me if [[Detroit]] artists were 'part of the [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] scene.' I said no. She seemed surprised. She pointed out that we are all in the [[GLMZ]]. I agreed. She said she had always thought of it as one thing. I said I understood why she thought that and that she was wrong.

The confusion is understandable. The consequences of the confusion are not. When media outlets use '[[GLMZ|Meridian 88]]' to mean all of [[GLMZ]], they collapse [[Detroit]] into a corridor with a specific geography, a specific infrastructure history, and a specific political identity — none of which is ours. [[Detroit]]'s east-bank location meant we were not connected to the 88th meridian build-out during the original zone construction. We were connected later, on worse terms, through political negotiations that gave the western bloc what it wanted and gave [[Detroit]] a transit link that [[Serathex|still]] runs slower than the main [[Iron Meridian Cooperative Backbone IMC-3 'Spine'|Spine]] by a margin that everyone in the zone knows about and the EZA has never explained. We are in [[GLMZ]] because the boundary was drawn to include us. We are not part of [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] because the corridor was not built for us and was not named with us in mind.

This is not a minor distinction. [[Detroit]] has its own history, its own civic identity, its own relationship to the zone that is not reducible to the western shore's narrative. [[The Renaissance Axis]], the [[Geartown]] campus, the east-bank manufacturing districts, [[Hamtramck Enclave|Hamtramck]], the Eight Mile Divide — these are not appendices to a [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] story. They are a separate story that shares a zone designation with [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] and has very little else in common with it.

I understand why western-shore residents use '[[GLMZ|Meridian 88]]' to mean everything they can see from the [[Iron Meridian Cooperative Backbone IMC-3 'Spine'|Spine]]. I am not asking them to stop. The name belongs to them and they are right to use it. I am asking the journalists, commentators, cultural critics, and anyone else who covers the [[GLMZ]] as a unified territory to understand that the zone is larger than the corridor, and that [[Detroit]] is not the eastern footnote of a western-shore story. We are our own story. We have always been our own story. We were our own story before the zone existed.

[[Detroit]] is [[GLMZ]]. [[Detroit]] is not [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]]. If you need to be told this more than once, you are not paying attention, and I am running out of patience for people who are not paying attention.
aftermath: The piece generated significant response in both Detroit media and corridor outlets. The Meridian Current reprinted it with a brief editorial note acknowledging the geographic distinction. Several corridor residents wrote responses arguing that 'Meridian 88' had evolved to mean GLMZ culturally, not just geographically — a position Osei-Winters addressed in a follow-up piece titled 'Cultural Evolution Is Not the Same as Being Right.'
runner_relevance: The Detroit-versus-Meridian-88 distinction has operational relevance in two specific contexts: Detroit-based clients are sensitive about the naming and will notice if a runner from the corridor uses the terms interchangeably — it signals that the runner doesn't know Detroit and hasn't done their homework. Separately, the east-bank transit infrastructure's slower speeds are a real operational constraint; travel times between Detroit and the Spine are longer than zone maps suggest, and operators who plan around western-corridor transit assumptions will arrive late.
